 What you’ll do 

 As a Senior GRC Engineer at Brex, you’ll lead the IT security compliance workstreams that connect our technical control owners to the people who examine our controls: external auditors, Internal Audit, state regulators, and Finance. You’ll coordinate and test the technical controls behind our financial reporting (SOX/ITGC), our annual SOC 1 Type 2 report, our state money transmitter examinations, and our FINRA IT requirements. You’ll also run the annual business continuity and disaster recovery (BC/DR) testing calendar.

 As part of the GRC team you may also contribute to the following operational tasks:

- Third party risk management 

- Risk register maintenance and reporting

- Customer Trust / GTM due diligence support

- Tooling access requests

- Assist with requests related to other certifications like SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, or ISO 27001

 Where you’ll work 

 This role will be based in our Seattle office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

 Responsibilities 

- Lead IT SOX/ITGC test procedures, walkthroughs, evidence, workpapers, and remediation across logical access, change management, computer operations, and IT governance.

- Manage our annual SOC 1 Type 2 engagement, including external auditor coordination, control descriptions, evidence, deficiency tracking, and review of draft report sections.

- Support state money transmitter (MTL) examinations by working with Legal, Compliance, and Finance on IT documentation, examiner requests, and tracking of IT findings.

- Test quarterly user access reviews, privileged-access evidence, and segregation-of-duties remediation, and verify that in-scope changes are complete and properly authorized.

- Run the annual BC/DR testing calendar, including tabletop and failover exercises, and document results, evidence, and remediation.

- Prepare FINRA-related IT control documentation, including business continuity, books-and-records, systems access reviews, and readiness testing.

- Track findings through to closure with clear control owners, deadlines, and evidence, and keep audit coordination separate from control operation.

- Support broader GRC team operational tasks related to evidence collection, access requests, and risk management.

 Requirements 

- 5+ years of experience in IT audit, SOX/ITGC testing, GRC, or technology compliance, in fintech, financial services, or public accounting.

- Hands-on experience with ITGC testing across logical access, change management, and computer operations, and with documenting results in audit workpapers.

- Working knowledge of SOC 1 / SSAE 18, including Type 2 reports, control descriptions, and deficiency management.

- Familiarity with PCAOB standards.

- Experience working with external auditors, regulators, or examiners and responding to their requests on deadline.

- Strong organization and project management skills, with the ability to run several audit workstreams on different calendars at once.

- Clear communication, and comfort holding technical control owners accountable for evidence and remediation.

 Bonus points 

- CISA, CIA, CPA, or CISSP certification.

- Experience with state money transmitter examinations or FINRA IT and books-and-records requirements.

- Experience coordinating BC/DR testing, including tabletop and failover exercises.

- Experience supporting audit readiness during an acquisition or integration.

- Familiarity with COSO 2013 and COBIT.

- Experience with GRC or audit workflow tools, or with SQL or scripting for control testing.

 Compensation

jobs.jd:
ABOUT THE TEAM
 The mission of the UI Test team is to ensure best-in-class UI experience for Rubrik products. The team accomplishes this by testing and automating customer workflows, providing UI automation infrastructure for end to end validation and benchmarking, checking usability and user experience and consistency across the features and products. Key stakeholders are product component teams, product management, release managers and end customers.

 The key responsibilities of the team include qualifying new features for production release and leading UI release regression qualification across Rubrik's on-prem and cloud products. We do manual and automated testing, including developing the test infrastructure needed. We build and use AI-native skills that automate the entire testing lifecycle, starting from generating the UI test plan to executing them in real environments. 

 ABOUT THE JOB 

 UI Test team responsibilities: 

- Feature qualification:

- The UI Test team qualifies new features from the end-user point of view (UI) for all Rubrik products before rolling out to production. We make sure every feature adheres to the quality standards and integrates well with the rest of the product. 

- Maintains high quality bar in test processes, strategy and test execution.

- Release regression testing: 

- 

- All released features are regression tested in every release, on a cadence that depends on the product, with both manual and automated UI testing.

- Automation: 

- New features enter the automation backlog after release and are picked up by priority. UI Automation using browser automation frameworks such as Playwright. 

- Infrastructure automation/maintenance using Python.

- Automated test pipelines in a CI/CD system

- Each phase of the testing life cycle is getting automated. Using AI-assisted tooling to generate test cases from product artifacts, execute them against real environments to reduce manual qualification effort.

 QUALIFICATIONS: 

- Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related field

- 5-8 years of experience in software testing, UI testing and automation

- Solid understanding on data protection, storage, security, virtualization, databases, cloud, kubernetes and generative AI

- Familiarity with UI performance and accessibility testing.

- Working knowledge of microservices, API, cloud native architectures and how to test them

- Experience with Cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), cybersecurity, AI resilience. A cloud certification is an advantage.

- Deep experience in driving complete test life cycle (test planning, execution, automation) and release qualification. Test management using TestRail or equivalent is a plus.

- Good hands-on experience programming in Python or equivalent and UI automation using TestIM, Selenium, Playwright or equivalent. JavaScript/TypeScript knowledge is a plus.

- Hands-on experience using AI coding or testing assistants in test authoring, debugging or automation, and sound judgment about the quality of their output.

- Hands on experience in creating, triaging and maintaining automated test pipeline using Jenkins, GitHub or similar CI/CD tools

- Strong written and verbal communication, including documentation that others can pick up without a handoff.

 Key differentiating factors: 

- Due to the unique placement of the team, it is exposed to multiple key technologies of Rubrik products. 

- This opportunity is not just another manual testing or automation role, key factor is the exposure and opportunity to learn core technologies of data protection, storage, security, anti ransomware, Virtualization(Hyper-V, VMware), Databases (SQL, Oracle, Mongo, DB2), cloud technologies (Azure, Google, AWS), Kubernetes, and cutting edge features involving Generative AI etc.

- Exposure to automated infrastructure creation and clean up on various platforms like VMware, Azure, AWS etc.

- Hands-on work with AI-based tools for test authoring, execution and automation.

- Automation using latest AI based tools 

- Every team member is given equal opportunity to lead releases on a rotational basis giving them opportunities to learn the release process and develop their leadership skills.

- Ownership opportunities: every member in the team irrespective of the designation has end-end ownership right from PRD review, test case development, interaction with key stakeholders( like Product manager, program managers, component managers and developers), execution and reporting

- Opportunity to become a quality advocate for the assigned component and product, and develop expertise in the assigned areas.

- This is a high visibility team as every feature of every product of the company has to be qualified by this team

jobs.jd:
We're transforming the grocery industry 

 At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. 

 Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

 Instacart is a Flex First team 

 There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work. 

 Overview 

 As a Staff Software Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping and advancing a robust data platform that addresses strategic challenges within Ads and across Instacart. You will design and build systems that capture and enforce data compliance requirements while enhancing self-service capabilities for internal consumers, all while maintaining strong guarantees around data integrity and consistency. By consolidating diverse requirements and collaborating across multiple engineering teams, you will help drive the platform’s north-star vision, ensuring strategic alignment and continuous delivery.

 You will be part of a dynamic team focused on transforming raw data into actionable insights for a wide range of stakeholders, including advertisers, data scientists, machine learning engineers, and sales teams. The team owns and operates critical systems such as metrics transformation and storage, billing, spam detection, and lift testing, supporting multiple facets of Instacart’s data infrastructure. Through this work, you will empower teams across the organization to make data-driven decisions and directly contribute to achieving key business outcomes.

 About the Job 

- Lead and break down complex problems while keeping the broader data vision in focus.

- Collaborate with engineers and engineering teams, providing mentorship and fostering a strong engineering culture.

- Directly contribute to our data vision and engineering architecture. Produce and review technical artifacts that align with business goals.

- Oversee engineering initiatives end-to-end, proactively managing risks, setting goals, and ensuring smooth execution and delivery.

- Balance maintainability with tech debt and the development of new features.

You'll own the full path from API request to running function. The APIs you build are the public surface of Lambda — high-throughput, strictly consistent, globally available — serving customers and CloudFormation alike. Behind those APIs, you'll design the asynchronous workflows that orchestrate a function's lifecycle: taking a customer's intent — a new function, a code deploy, a version publish — and propagating it safely to the systems that actually execute functions. That means solving metadata propagation at global scale: ensuring every configuration change reaches the right compute fleet, in the right region, with the right ordering guarantees, even under partial failures.

We operate at the scale of one of the largest services in AWS. Availability is a first-class design constraint, not an afterthought.

What we're looking for

jobs.title: Principal Engineer Capacity/Compute
jobs.location: Seattle, WA | San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.jd:
About Anthropic 

 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

 About the Role 

 Anthropic manages one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry — spanning multiple accelerator families, cpu families and clouds. The Capacity Engineering team is responsible for making sure all our infrastructure resources are accounted for, well-utilized, and efficiently allocated. We own the data, tooling, and operational systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization across first-party and third-party compute.

 As an engineer on Capacity Engineering, you will build the production systems that power this work: data pipelines that ingest and normalize telemetry from heterogeneous cloud environments, observability tooling that gives the org real-time visibility into fleet health, and performance instrumentation that measures how efficiently every major workload uses the hardware it’s running on. You will be expected to write production-quality code every day, operate alongside Kubernetes-native infrastructure at meaningful scale, and directly influence decisions around one of Anthropic’s largest areas of spend.

 You’ll collaborate closely with research engineering, infrastructure, inference, and finance teams. The work requires someone who can move between data engineering, systems engineering, and observability with comfort — and who thrives in a high-autonomy, high-ambiguity environment.

 This is a pipeline role feeding four areas. Depending on your background and business priority, you’ll focus primarily in one, but the boundaries are fluid and the problems overlap: 

- Data platform Pipelines that ingest occupancy and utilization telemetry from Kubernetes clusters, normalize billing and usage across cloud providers, and serve the BigQuery tables the rest of the org queries against. Correctness, completeness, and latency are the job, not a footnote. Consumers range from research engineers to finance to leadership, so it's product work as much as engineering: defining schema contracts, making data discoverable, and figuring out what people actually need.

- Planning Knowing what the fleet has, where it's going, and what's in the way. Making the state of the fleet legible and actionable in real time: cluster health tooling, capacity planning platforms, alerting on occupancy drops and allocation problems, and systemic fixes to scheduling and fragmentation. Kubernetes operations on one side, cross-team coordination on the other.

- Efficiency Measuring and improving how effectively every major workload uses the hardware it runs on. Instrumenting utilization across training, inference, and eval systems, building benchmarking infrastructure, establishing per-config baselines, and working directly with system-owning teams to close the gaps. The metric has to be good enough that the team on the hook for it agrees with the number.

- Attribution and forecasting Connecting what the fleet costs to what the business is doing with it. Reconciling CSP billing exports against vendor telemetry and internal systems with mismatched schemas, attributing spend to the workloads and teams that generate it, and turning inference demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan. Efficiency metrics have to survive contact with finance: stripped of pure demand and unit-price effects, reproducible month over month, and legible to a CFO.

 Key responsibilities 

- Build the planning and allocation stack — the tools leadership uses to allocate capacity, teams use to plan against their allocations, and the scheduler enforces. Cross-region and cross-provider placement, guardrails, queueing, occupancy KPIs.

- Drive the efficiency programs: stranding and rightsizing, unused capacity recovery, and job-level utilization across training, inference, and eval. Establish per-config baselines and work with system-owning teams to close the gaps. Utilization improvements are worth enormous sums at our scale.

- Own attribution and forecasting — reconcile billing across ten-plus providers against telemetry and internal systems, attribute spend to the workloads that generate it, and turn demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan and supply pipeline.

- Build the data platform underneath all of it: pipelines ingesting occupancy, utilization, and cost from a rapidly diversifying fleet into BigQuery, with real ownership of completeness, latency SLOs, and gap detection. Every new provider is a net-new integration.

- Operate Kubernetes-native systems at scale — collection agents, workload labeling, and the taint/reservation/scheduling behavior that determines what capacity is actually usable.

- Treat the output as a product, not a pipeline. Gather your own requirements, define schema contracts, and design for consumers ranging from research engineers to a CFO — including on-call and SLOs, because these surfaces are load-bearing for the company.

 What you bring 

- A strong track record building and operating production systems. This is a hands-on engineering role with a devops flavor.

- Python and SQL at production quality. Most pipeline code is Python; the presentation layer is BigQuery SQL, including table-valued functions and views. Both need to be idiomatic, well-tested, and maintainable.

- Deep experience with at least one major cloud provider (Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure) and its operations

- Experience with observability tooling stack, including Prometheus, PromQL, and Grafana, including writing recording rules and building monitoring that engineering teams rely on.

- Ability to gather your own requirements and work across organizational b

This is Adyen 

 Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for global customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft, making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition. We create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by a culture that encourages ownership and provides the support to truly own your career. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team, delivering innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster.

 Data Foundations 

 Adyen is building a top-tier data team across San Francisco and Amsterdam. The goal is to accelerate data as our most differentiating and least replicable asset across our company. We are focusing on the foundations: the things that make data work as one thing. We decide how it fits together, what it means, and how anyone, human or AI, can trust and use it.

 The team is new and sits at the heart of our engineering organization. You will join as one of its technical leaders. You will architect data and work on complex challenges across the company, multiplying your impact through the teams and people you work with. You win them over with good design, working prototypes and trust. By driving decisions through ambiguity, you will shape the next generation of Ayden's data.

 You will be based in San Francisco and work closely with the Data Foundations lead in Amsterdam. You will have a lot of room to run your own week.

 What you will do 

- Build greenfield. The mandate, the architecture and the standards are being written now. You help write them.

- Design the foundation. Set the target architecture for shared data models, data contracts and the semantic layer that every domain builds on.

- Give every metric one clear meaning. Work with domain teams so each core metric is defined once and owned by the domain that creates it. Variants get their own names.

- Make data contracts the norm. Agree contracts between producers and consumers, with owners, versions and automatic checks. Consumers are never surprised.

- Build lineage in from the start. Anyone can trace a figure to its source without asking the engineer who built the pipeline.

- Help teams ship data products. Guide domain teams to publish datasets with a clear owner, schema and service level. They own the product. You own the standard.

- Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, review designs and solve hard problems in the data stack.

- Partner across Adyen. Product, Finance, Compliance, Platform Engineering and domain leads. Win the argument with data and a working prototype.

- Grow other engineers. Mentor engineers in Data Foundations and in the domains. Help them solve problems with their own ideas, and raise the bar in design reviews.

 Who you are 

- You have 10+ years in data engineering or data architecture, and you have worked at Staff scope. You have set direction for more than one team, and you are still hands on.

- You pick your own problems. You see what needs to change and drive it to done without being told.

- You have designed shared data models, data contracts or semantic layers that many teams build on, and you can defend the trade-offs.

- You have changed what other teams built without any authority over them. You did it with data, prototypes and trust.

- You explain hard ideas in plain words to engineers, finance people and executives. You write clearly.

- You work well with Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance and other stakeholders, across time zones.

Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose of economic empowerment. The blocks that form our foundational teams — People, Finance, Counsel, Hardware, Information Security, Platform Infrastructure Engineering, and more — provide support and guidance at the corporate level. They work across business groups and around the globe, spanning time zones and disciplines to develop inclusive People policies, forecast finances, give legal counsel, safeguard systems, nurture new initiatives, and more. Every challenge creates possibilities, and we need different perspectives to see them all. Bring yours to Block.

 About the role 

 More and more of our engineering work now runs through autonomous agents, and those agents can only be as effective as the tools, context, and codebase around them. As a Developer Experience Engineer, you'll build the tooling and agent workflows that let humans and agents change our largest monorepos quickly and safely.

 You'll own the interfaces engineers use to observe, steer, and give context to the agents working on our code. You'll also build the guardrails that keep complexity in check as those agents take on bigger changes. Large-scale work like framework upgrades, language migrations, and dependency health is still part of the job, but you'll do it by building and steering agents rather than making the changes by hand. This is a high-leverage role. Every improvement you ship multiplies across the whole engineering organization.

 What you’ll do 

- Build and ship the tools engineers and their agents use every day, such as CLIs, desktop integrations, and interfaces for observing, unblocking, and steering autonomous agents, and own their adoption, distribution, and support

- Design and evolve agentic loops (the plan, act, verify, and iterate cycles) and the harnesses, skills, and context that let agents do real engineering work reliably

- Build agent workflows that drive large-scale changes across the codebase, including framework upgrades, language migrations, and dependency updates, with minimal disruption to product teams

- Build the guardrails, tests, and automation that make large, agent-authored changes safe to land, and track the leading indicators of growing complexity

- Find friction in the development workflow for both humans and agents, and fix the root causes

- Partner with builders inside and outside of engineering to understand their pain points, and measure the adoption and impact of what you ship

- Set technical direction and mentor other engineers on agent design, tooling, and codebase health

 What we’re looking for 

 We care more about what you've done than about which specific technologies you used to do it.

 Required 

- Shipping developer tooling at scale: You've shipped tools that engineers use daily, such as CLIs, desktop integrations, configuration management, or internal platforms. You understand what it takes to drive adoption, debug problems, and support users.

- Scaling work with agents: You've built agent workflows that finished work that would normally take a team weeks. Examples include generating codebase summaries or world models, writing skills and loops, or orchestrating a team of semi-deterministic agents. You have a deep understanding of agentic loops (tool use, context management, verification, failure handling) and are eager to keep evolving them as the field changes.

- Evolving frameworks and large codebases: You have deep experience with application or platform frameworks, including upgrading them and managing their evolution over time. You also have a track record of leading migrations or large refactors from planning through rollout.

- Significant experience (typically 10+ years for Staff, 7+ for Senior) working in large, complex codebases

- Strong communication skills and the ability to build trust with teams by owning the outcomes of your work

 Nice to have 

- Experience with harness engineering or context engineering

- Experience with agent observability, for example through OpenTelemetry

- Experience distributing internal tools (versioning, release channels, auto-update) and measuring adoption with telemetry or surveys

- Background in developer productivity metrics, test infrastructure, or CI/CD

- A passion for intuitive user experience and good taste in elegant solutions

- Open source contributions to developer tooling or agent frameworks

 Block takes a market-based approach to pay, and pay may vary depending on your location. U.S. locations are categorized into one of four zones based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. The successful candidate’s starting pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future.

jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.jd:
About Anthropic 

 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

 About the role 

 As a Senior Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.

 The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

 You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

 We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.

 The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time. 

 What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.

 This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

 Key responsibilities 

- 
 Design, build, and maintain biology software in genomics and structural biology (libraries, command-line tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks) for use by researchers and AI agents, inside Anthropic and externally

- 
 Own the path from research code to public release, including testing, validation against reference data and established tools, benchmarking, documentation, and packaging, and make the call on when something is ready to ship

- 
 Maintain what we release: triage issues, review outside contributions, and manage breaking changes

- 
 Represent the team in the biology community through conferences, workshops, tutorials, and direct work with researchers and maintainers, and turn what you learn about their needs into priorities for the team

- 
 Partner with the team's computational and experimental scientists to turn research code into well-tested, reusable software

- 
 Lead the technical direction of the projects you own through design review, code review, and mentoring, and, depending on your interests and the team's needs, lead a small team

- 
 Build with Claude and AI coding agents as your default way of working, hold agent-written code to the same standard as your own, and set the team's practices for reviewing and validating it

 Minimum qualifications 

- 
 Have built, released, and maintained biology software that researchers outside your own group use, with evidence of adoption you can point to (for example public repositories, package downloads, citations, or use in other groups' pipelines)

- 
 Have deep working expertise in genomics or structural biology, including the data types, file formats, standard tools, and common failure modes of at least one of these fields

- 
 Are proficient in Python and comfortable working with large datasets in Linux and cloud or cluster computing environments

- 
 Practice rigorous testing and release engineering: unit and integration tests, continuous integration, validation against reference data, packaging, and versioning

- 
 Use AI coding tools as a central part of how you build software, and can show how you verify the correctness and performance of code you did not write by hand

- 
 Have led a technical project with multiple contributors, setting direction and reviewing others' work while continuing to write code yourself

- 
 Can explain technical work clearly to both biologists and engineers, in writing (documentation, tutorials) and in person (talks, workshops)

 Preferred qualifications 

- 
 Depth in both genomics and structural biology

- 
 A record as the creator or a core maintainer of a widely used open-source tool in computational biology

- 
 Experience managing or formally leading a team of engineers or scientists

- 
 A graduate degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent experience

- 
 Proficiency in a systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and experience with performance work on large biological datasets

- 
 Experience building software in other areas of computational biology, such as phylogenetics, proteomics, cheminformatics, or high-throughput screen analysis

jobs.title: Power Platform Developer - SaaS Automation & Integration, Charles River Development, Assistant Vice President
jobs.jd:
Role Overview 
 We are seeking an experienced Power Platform Developer, with at least 5 years experience in a similar role, to join our SaaS organisation, developing automation, integration, reporting and operational capabilities across our technology ecosystem. 
 The role sits at the intersection of Power Platform development, DevOps, SaaS operations, data engineering and API integration. The successful candidate will build solutions that reduce manual operational activity, improve service visibility, integrate enterprise platforms and provide actionable operational intelligence. 
 This is a hands-on engineering role requiring strong Power Platform expertise together with scripting, SQL, REST API and infrastructure automation skills. 

 Key Responsibilities 
 Power Platform & Automation 
 
- Design, develop and support solutions using Microsoft Power Platform. 
 
- Build production-grade Power Automate workflows for operational and business process automation. 
 
- Integrate Power Automate with internal and external platforms using REST APIs, custom connectors and authenticated API calls. 
 
- Develop reusable automation components and integration patterns. 
 
- Troubleshoot failed workflows, API interactions and automation dependencies. 
 
- Apply appropriate source control, testing, deployment and lifecycle-management practices. 
 
 Power BI & Data 
 
- Design and maintain Power BI datasets, semantic models, reports and dashboards. 
 
- Use the Power BI REST API to automate administration, reporting, refresh and integration activities. 
 
- Develop data extraction and transformation processes using T-SQL and Python. 
 
- Combine data from operational SaaS platforms and APIs to provide service, operational and management reporting. 
 
- Develop appropriate data models, measures and transformations to support scalable reporting. 
 
 Desirable Experience 
 
- API & Systems Integration: Designing REST API integrations with JIRA, ServiceNow, Salesforce and OpsRamp. 

- Python & PowerShell: Building secure, resilient automation for APIs, data, administration, reporting and scheduled workflows. 

- Ansible & Infrastructure Automation: Building production-ready Ansible automation integrated with Power Platform, Python, PowerShell and APIs. 

- DevOps & Source Control: Managing automation through Git, peer review, CI/CD, documentation and audit controls. 
 
 SaaS / Operational Mindset 
 We are particularly looking for someone who understands that production automation must be engineered as a service, not simply written as a script. 
 The successful candidate will: 
 
- Automate repetitive operational activity. 
 
- Engineer for reliability and recoverability. 
 
- Understand the production impact of failed workflows. 
 
- Prefer reusable APIs and automation components over manual processes. 
 
- Design with security and least privilege in mind. 
 
- Identify opportunities for systemic automation rather than repeatedly solving individual operational incidents. 
 
 Candidate Profile 
 
- You will be a strong fit if you are a developer who enjoys connecting systems together. 

- You should be equally comfortable building a Power Automate workflow, querying data with T-SQL, consuming an API with Python, writing a PowerShell automation, triggering Ansible automation and investigating the resulting service behaviour in Dynatrace. 

- This breadth is important. The role requires someone capable of understanding an operational requirement end-to-end and selecting the most appropriate technology rather than attempting to solve every requirement with Power Platform alone. 

 About State Street 

 Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.

 We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.

jobs.jd:
Every team has AI. Few have mastered it. Humans were built to adapt, but AI is now moving faster than most workforces can.

Multiverse is the AI adoption layer: the missing link between the AI tools that companies have invested in and the people expected to use them.

Our ambition is to put AI capability in every worker’s hands. Apprenticeships got us started: we’ve trained over a third of the UK’s data and AI apprentices, worked with a third of the FTSE 100, and generated £2bn+ in verified ROI. Now Mastry, our new adaptive learning platform, takes that further, guiding a company’s AI workforce transformation from start to finish. Mae, our AI guide inside Mastry, is a real-time AI agent that thinks, speaks, listens and sees, working alongside the tools you already use, like Claude and Copilot.

We closed our latest fundraising round in April 2026, with $500m+ raised in total from VC partners including Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Schroders Capital and Lightspeed. With a $2.1bn valuation, we are Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn, and we are just getting started.

If you want to shape how the workforce wins in the AI era, come and join us.


SENIOR AI ENGINEER - SECURITY

Multiverse is the upskilling platform for AI and Technology adoption.

We have partnered with 1,500+ companies to deliver a new kind of learning that's transforming today's workforce.

Our upskilling apprenticeships are designed for people of any age and career stage to build critical AI, data, and tech skills. Our learners have driven $2bn+ ROI for their employers, using the skills they've learned to improve productivity and measurable performance.

In April 2026, we announced $70 million in strategic funding, led by Schroders Capital, with participation from StepStone Group, Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst. At an increased valuation of $2.1bn, the round makes us Europe's first EdTech double unicorn.

But we aren't stopping there. With a strong operational footprint and 800+ employees, we have ambitious plans to continue scaling. We're building a world where tech skills unlock people's potential and output.

Join Multiverse and power our mission to equip the workforce to win in the AI era.




THE AGENTIC WORK ENVIRONMENT TEAM

The Agentic Work Environment (AWE) owns the environment everyone at Multiverse works in, wherever they are in the world. That covers the devices, workplace tools and accounts colleagues use every day, the platform our product is built and run on, and the identity and access that decide who, or which agent, can do what across all of it. Product teams own what they build; we own the ground it stands on, the path it takes to production, and the baseline standards it meets on the way. Our mission is to make the safe way the fast way for every colleague and the agents they put to work.

For a security-minded AI engineer, that remit runs in two directions. In the product platform, you build security into the path itself: review agents that check every change against our baseline standards, one identity for customers, staff and agents, and detection and response through our SIEM and SOAR, so nobody, person or agent, has to remember to be secure. In the workplace, you secure the devices, tools and accounts colleagues around the world rely on. As more of them put agents to work, whatever their job title, you make sure every agent has its own identity, a named owner, scoped access and evals, so autonomy is earned on evidence rather than granted on trust.




WHAT YOUR DAY-TO-DAY WILL LOOK LIKE



Every day will be different, but you can expect it to include:

Build security into the path to production. You turn our baseline standards into checks that run on every change: policy as code, review agents that check each change against the baseline and a team's own standards, and gates matched to the risk of what's changing. Staying on the path should meet the security requirements without any extra work.

Secure the agents we and our colleagues build. You threat-model agent systems end to end, from prompt injection and tool misuse to data leaking through context and retrieval, and design the controls that stop it: scoped tool permissions, permission-aware retrieval, sandboxing, and human approval where the risk calls for it.

Give every agent an identity. You build the identity and access layer for agents. Each one has its own identity, a named owner, least-privilege access that is reviewed and can be revoked at once, and a full record of what it did.

Build detection and response with agents. You write detections and automated responses on our SIEM and SOAR, and build agents that triage alerts, gather context and carry out bounded, reversible responses, so people spend their time on the cases that need judgement.

Secure the workplace, worldwide. You apply the same approach to the devices, workplace tools and accounts colleagues use every day: automated controls rather than manual checklists, and access that is granted and removed as people join, move and leave.

Prove it holds with security evals. You build eval pipelines and red-team exercises that show whether our agents and controls stand up to attack, and produce compliance evidence as a by-product of the work rather than as screenshots for an auditor.

Influence technical direction. You have opinions about how things should be built, and you back them up with evidence. You contribute to architectural decisions, push back when the team is heading in the wrong direction, and propose better approaches.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Security Engineering: You have built security into systems rather than reviewed it after the fact, across some mix of application and cloud security, identity and access, and detection and response. You understand how AI systems get attacked, through prompt injection, tool misuse and data leaking through context, and you design controls that make the secure option the easy one for the people using them

Plaid's Connectivity team builds and operates the network that powers open finance, connecting consumers' financial accounts to the apps and services they choose to use across thousands of institutions. Where an institution offers an API, we use it. Where one doesn't, we still need a dependable, secure way to honor a consumer's request to share their own data. You will set its direction and build the systems yourself: browser- and mobile-based clients that act on the consumer's behalf, the network egress infrastructure those sessions run through, credential and session handling, and the measurement that tells us how well it all works.

Institutions' traffic controls often cannot distinguish a consumer-directed session from unwanted automation. You will study how real clients behave at the browser, device and network level, and make permissioned sessions faithful to that behavior so that consumers' connections stay reliable as institutions change.

You will turn today's approach into a platform that can be extended to new institutions in weeks, decide where to build versus buy, and partner closely with Legal, Policy, Security and Product so that every method we deploy is one we're confident in.  - You'll instrument success rate, breakage detection and time to repair, and drive staged rollouts with Product and Account Management.

 - You'll write the design and risk documentation that lets leadership make deployment decisions, and bring Legal, Policy and Security in early.

Qualifications:

 - 6+ years of software engineering experience, including hands-on work building and operating systems that act on a user's behalf against third-party web or mobile applications at scale.

 - Deep knowledge of browser internals and automation (Chromium, Chrome DevTools Protocol, Playwright or Puppeteer) or of mobile application internals and instrumentation.

About Citi: 
 Citi, the leading global bank, has approximately 200 million customer accounts and does business in more than 160 countries and jurisdictions. Citi provides consumers, corporations, governments, and institutions with a broad range of financial products and services, including consumer banking and credit, corporate and investment banking, securities brokerage, transaction services, and wealth management.
 
 As a bank with a brain and a soul, Citi creates economic value that is systemically responsible and in our clients’ best interests. As a financial institution that touches every region of the world and every sector that shapes your daily life, our Operations & Technology teams are charged with a mission that rivals any large tech company. Our technology solutions are the foundations of everything we do from keeping the bank safe, managing global resources, and providing the technical tools our workers need to be successful to designing our digital architecture and ensuring our platforms provide a first-class customer experience. We reimagine client and partner experiences to deliver excellence through secure, reliable, and efficient services.
 
 Our commitment to diversity includes a workforce that represents the clients we serve from all walks of life, backgrounds, and origins. We foster an environment where the best people want to work. We value and demand respect for others, promote individuals based on merit, and ensure opportunities for personal development are widely available to all. Ideal candidates are innovators with well-rounded backgrounds who bring their authentic selves to work and complement our culture of delivering results with pride. If you are a problem solver who seeks passion in your work, come join us. We’ll enable growth and progress together.

 The Team: 
 The Startups & Partnerships team is the forward scout of the Citi's Head of AI Organization . Our mandate: identify, evaluate, and rapidly onboard the emerging technologies that will define Citi's next chapter with Artificial Intelligence as our number one strategic priority right now. We don't sit in a lab waiting for ideas to trickle in. We move across every line of business at Citi, sit down directly with business stakeholders and clients, and go toe-to-toe with the sharpest startups and frontier AI labs in the market. We run fast, we run lean, and we run with the full weight of a global institution behind us.

 The Opportunity: 
 As an AI Engineer on the Startups & Partnerships team, you will be at the tip of the spear for Citi's AI strategy - building, testing, and shipping real applications that touch real business problems across the bank, not writing whitepapers about them from the sidelines.
 You'll get a level of exposure that's rare in a Tier-1 global bank: direct access to business requirements, hands-on evaluation of the newest models and platforms from the industry's leading AI labs, and the mandate to move at startup speed inside an institution operating at global scale. If you want to build things that matter, get them in front of real users fast, and shape how one of the world's largest financial institutions adopts AI - this is the seat.

 What You'll Do Day to Day 
 
- Build and ship AI applications - architect, develop, and deploy production-grade AI-powered tools, pipelines, and workflows that solve real business problems across Citi's lines of business.
 
- Evaluate emerging AI technology - run structured proof-of-concepts and sandbox "bake-offs" to rapidly assess new models, platforms, and startup tools (LLMs, agentic frameworks, orchestration layers) for real-world fit.
 
- Prototype at speed - turn a business idea into a working demo in days, not quarters, and iterate quickly based on stakeholder feedback.
 
- Integrate across the stack - connect LLMs and agentic systems to enterprise APIs, data pipelines, and lightweight front-end or tooling layers to deliver end-to-end working solutions.
 
- Deliver PoCs into production pathways - work with governance, risk, and platform teams to shepherd validated solutions from prototype toward scaled deployment.
 
- Communicate impact - translate technical work into clear, compelling narratives for senior business and technology stakeholders.

 Required Skills 
 
- A full-stack engineer with applied AI/LLM experience - this is explicitly not a data science or ML research role. We need builders, not modelers.
 
- Proven experience building and shipping AI applications, pipelines, and workflows in live, production environments - not just notebooks and academic experiments.
 
- Hands-on proficiency with Large Language Models (LLMs) , prompt engineering, and agentic frameworks and orchestration tools (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, or similar).
 
- Strong software engineering fundamentals - comfortable working across the stack, from backend services and API integrations to lightweight front-end or internal tooling layers.
 
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills - you can work directly with business leaders and clients, not just other engineers.
 
- A track record of learning and adopting new tools and platforms quickly as the AI landscape evolves.
 
- Comfort operating in a large, regulated, global institution while bringing a startup-speed mentality to your work.

 Nice-to-Have Skills 
 
- Experience working directly with startups, venture teams, or technology scouting functions.
 
- Familiarity with vector databases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), or knowledge graph-based retrieval.
 
- Experience with containerization and cloud-native deployment (Docker, Kubernetes) for AI services.
 
- Prior exposure to financial services, banking, or other highly regulated industries.
 
- Experience presenting technical concepts to non-technical, senior business audiences.

- Bachelor’s degree/University degree or equivalent experience

- Master’s degree preferred

jobs.jd:
What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better. 

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally. 



The Role:  

As a Software Engineer within our Billing group, you will play a key role in developing core areas of our new billing platform. You’ll provide world-class experiences to thousands of customers who use and trust Paddle every day. You'll take the lead on discovering new features, planning their implementation, and contributing your technical expertise to shape the future of our billing platform.

You’ll collaborate with multiple teams—engineers, product managers, and designers—working across a wide range of areas that will give you plenty of opportunities to develop your skills and grow your career as a valued member of our engineering team.



What you'll do: 

 - Independently deliver on milestones that may span across multiple systems within Billing.

 - Make changes with care and precision, recognising the importance of correctness when working with financial data.

 - Contribute to systems designed for scale, reliability, and security, following established architectural patterns.

 - Write clear, well-structured, and well-tested code that meets team standards.

 - Participate in code reviews, both giving and receiving constructive feedback.

 - Work closely with other engineers, product managers, and designers to understand requirements and deliver solutions.

 - Break down larger pieces of work into manageable tasks and estimate your own work with guidance.

 - Help monitor and support production services, investigating and fixing issues as they arise.

 - Contribute to shaping our team and wider engineering culture to ensure Paddle remains an exceptional place to work.

 - Work closely with Product Managers, Designers, Data, Risk, and Operations to translate business requirements into robust technical solutions.

 - Help shape product direction by providing technical insights, trade-offs, and delivery estimates.

 - Partner with Customer Support or Operations teams to investigate and resolve production issues.



We'd love to hear from you if you:

 - You have a development background with Go.

 - Have experience designing and building systems to handle high traffic at scale in a cloud-based environment in AWS

 - Are someone who enjoys collaborating with our technical and non-technical departments

 - Have a proactive attitude towards finding ways to improve the code and team processes.

 - A strong understanding of the development process - from design through to deployment, maintenance, and what that means for day-to-day development.

 - A strong understanding of API principles and best practices.

 - A proven track record of bias for action and strong customer focus.

 - Solid communication and collaboration skills, you should be comfortable working alongside both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Are someone who takes pride in what you build.



Everyone is welcome at Paddle

At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer, we don’t care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you’re from. We’re more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you’ll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t match every part of the job ad, especially if you’re part of an underrepresented group.

Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We’re committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let’s grow together.

 

Why you’ll love working at Paddle

We’re a diverse, growing group of Paddlers who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.

We live and breathe our values, which are:

 - Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us”

 - Paddle Simply - “Simple can be harder than complex: you have to get your thinking clean to make it simple”

 - Paddle for others - “We can realise our wildest dreams, so long as we help enough other people to realise theirs”

 

We offer a full suite of benefits, including attractive salaries, stock options, unlimited holidays, enhanced parental leave, retirement plans, private healthcare and well-being initiatives.

 

We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.

 

Connecting at Paddle

We’re a ‘digital-first’ company, which means our Paddlers always have the freedom to choose where, when and how they work within our hub locations.

We recognize that where our Paddlers do their best work is unique to them and we provide trust and autonomy for everyone to work in a way which fits them best. We also value the power of connection and have invested in global hubs which help local communities flourish and bring us together for focused collaboration.

 

Our Paddle hubs:

 - In Europe: UK (London headquarters), Portugal (Lisbon hub), Netherlands and Ireland (Dublin hub)

 - In North America: Austin, TX (USA) and Toronto (Canada)

 - In APAC: Singapore

Our hub philosophy creates an engaging experience for all Paddlers, wherever, whenever and however we choose to work.

The Company 
 
 PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy. 
 
 We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.
 
 We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade. 
 
 Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.
